SHAP values for a prediction model

Source: R/pred-shap.R
wgh_shap.Rd

Computes SHAP values for the rows of X. For XGBoost models exact TreeSHAP contributions are used. For any other model, exact kernel SHAP (kernelshap) is computed with an explicit background sample, which the explainable growth prediction study (Ho 2026, manuscript under review) used for quantile regression models.

Usage

wgh_shap(object, X, bg_X = NULL, pred_fun = NULL, feature_names = NULL)

Arguments

object

A fitted model.

X

Data frame (or matrix for XGBoost) of rows to explain.

bg_X

Background data (rows representing the population). Ignored for XGBoost.

pred_fun

Prediction function function(object, newdata) returning a numeric vector. Defaults to predict().

feature_names

Features to explain (default all columns of X).

Value

An object of class wgh_shap with the SHAP matrix S, the explained data X and the baseline.

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- lm(height ~ age + baz, data = growdat)
X <- growdat[1:100, c("age", "baz")]
sh <- wgh_shap(fit, X, bg_X = growdat[sample(nrow(growdat), 50), c("age", "baz")])
wgh_shap_summary(sh)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   feature mean_abs_shap  rank
#>   <chr>           <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 age            22.2       1
#> 2 baz             0.975     2
# }
